messages:
neil: Heads-up — we need to lock down a canonical benchmark methodology for quantized runs (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit). Perf team is seeing high variance across PRs, especially when calibration and kernel selection are involved. Key axes: warmup, power limits, tokenization, kernel selection, KV cache priming, and how we report steady-state vs calibration costs.

maya: +1. Can we be concrete on the warmup story? Right now some runs use 50 steps, others 500. That skews comparisons, esp for FP8 where kernels JIT and calibration can add one-time costs.

sam: Proposal: separate phases in every run -> (1) calibration-only (one-shot) with timing, (2) warmup with KV priming (fixed # tokens), (3) steady-state measurement. Report each number separately.

alicia: Also enforce GPU power limits and clock state. We've seen 8-12% variance if the card is in auto boost. Use `nvidia-smi -pm 1; nvidia-smi -pl <watts>` and record `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,clocks.gr,clocks.mem --format=csv`.

maya: Agree. For warmup we suggest: run 2000 tokens of generated text (or 200 steps) or until the latency/throughput stabilizes within 3% over a sliding window. Document the metric.

sam: Kernel selection detail: runtime should log chosen kernels per layer and per sequence length. FP8 kernels sometimes fall back to mixed kernels for some ops; that fallback cost must be visible. Add a small CSV: `layer,op,kernel,ms_per_token` in the run artifact.

dena: KV cache note: make sure the benchmark harness exercises both cache-hit and cache-miss scenarios. For cache-hit steady-state, we should prime with a 2048 token prefix for long-context runs, then measure only generation steps. Otherwise results are misleading.

maya: Calibration effects: run calibration as a distinct step and report calibration_time_seconds and calibration_memory_peak. Example: "calibration_time_seconds": "42.3" for int8 on 8 layers sampled. This should not be counted in steady-state throughput.

sam: Example command we propose for reproducibility:
```
./bench/run_quant_bench \
  --model gpt2-xl \
  --quant int8 \
  --batch 4 \
  --seq 512 \
  --warmup_tokens 2000 \
  --measure_tokens 50000 \
  --power_limit 220 \
  --log-kernels csv \
  --seed 42
```

neil: Nice. Also ensure tokenization is fixed — same tokenizer version, vocab, and preproc script. Differences in whitespace handling change token counts and can bias per-token throughput. Record tokenizer git sha in artifacts.

alicia: CI-wise: add a nightly job that runs reduced-size config (e.g., 1/10 measure_tokens) for FP8/INT8/4bit and fails if throughput regresses >8% vs baseline. Use pinned driver + CUDA + cuDNN versions.

dena: Quick empirical numbers from today (non-ideal env): FP8 steady-state ~12k tok/s, INT8 ~9.1k tok/s, 4-bit ~7.4k tok/s. But calibration added ~25s and first 100 tokens were slower by ~18% on FP8 because of kernel priming.

maya: For batching heuristics: test fixed-batch (N) vs dynamic batching with max_delay_ms. Report p50/p95 latency and throughput for each. In dynamic mode, also report effective batch size distribution.

sam: Perf regression root-cause pattern we've seen: a change in kernel selection logic caused extra memcpy on int8 path for odd sequence lengths. Recommend adding a regression test that runs seq lengths 1..1024 and asserts no unexpected memcpy events in the hot path.

neil: Action items: sam -> update bench harness to split phases + kernel logs. maya -> standardize calibration script + tokenizer SHA. alicia -> CI job + power/driver pinning. dena -> collect baseline artifacts and publish to /bench/artifacts/quant_baseline/1769804321.

perf-bot: Automated note: create ticket PERF-quant-bench-1769804321 with attachments: run_template, example_artifact_schema, ci_job_spec.

neil: Thanks everyone — let's aim to have updated harness + one canonical FP8/INT8/4bit baseline by EOD Friday. If you disagree with any part, reply here with specifics. :thumbsup:
